items.label: text
items.text: Molybdenite is an ore of molybdenum. The mineral it contains is MoS2.

items.label: text
items.text: The following set of reactions are used to produce pure molybdenum(Vl) oxide (MoO₃), from which molybdenum metal can be obtained.

items.label: text
items.text: The ore is first roasted in air to form MoO₃. The equation for this reaction is:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 M o S _ { 2 } ( s ) + 7 O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 M o O _ { 3 } ( s ) + 4 S O _ { 2 } ( g ) \dots 1

items.label: text
items.text: The crude compound is now heated with concentrated ammonia solution:

items.label: formula
items.text: M o O _ { 3 } ( s ) + 2 N H _ { 3 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } O ( I ) \rightarrow ( N H _ { 4 } ) M o O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \dots 2

items.label: text
items.text: Ammonium molybdate is crystallised from the solution and when these crystals are heated pure MoO₃ is formed:

items.label: text
items.text: The molybdenum can be extracted from MoO₃ by heating with carbon.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Explain the meaning of the word ore.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Put ticks in the appropriate boxes in the table to classify each of the reactions 1 and 3 above. Each reaction type may occur once, twice or not at all.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Molybdenum(Vl) oxide can be heated with carbon to form molybdenum metal. The other product of the reaction is carbon monoxide. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: d Explain which substance is the reducing agent when molybdenum(Vl) oxide is heated with carbon. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain what the reaction in c suggests about the position of molybdenum in the reactivity series. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: Molybdenum can also be extracted from MoO₃ by heating with aluminium. Use your knowledge of the reactivity series to give a reason why this method is more expensive than heating with carbon. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: g Describe a chemical test you could use to show that the product of reaction 2 contains ammonium ions. (2)

items.text: This question is about lead(ll) iodide. This is a bright yellow substance that is insoluble in water. In the past it was used as a pigment, but due to its toxicity this no longer happens. It is now used in the development of new types of solar cell.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe a method a student could use to produce a pure, dry sample of lead(IIl) iodide. (5)
